note: No source gives a construction or first-occupation date for Wilca. The English article is a one-sentence stub with no date, and the Spanish article describes the terraces, the circular structures of stone slabs and the access route in detail but never states a year, century or millennium for the site. The field stays empty.

Wikipedia gives no coordinates for the Mulri Hills (a coord-missing notice) and places them only in Gulshan Town, Karachi, in front of Karachi University; the one map point found (an OpenStreetMap-derived hill node 4 km from the stored point) is not a source that prints a quotable point for the site.
Wikipedia names only the periods (Late Palaeolithic and Mesolithic) of the flint scatters found on the Mulri Hills; a period word gives no start year or century.

No source prints a point for the Anavarza theatre itself. Wikidata Q29002435 gives 37°14'38.400"N, 35°53'42.000"E = 37.2439, 35.8950 for the Anazarbus amphitheatre, 0.73 km from the stored point, but an amphitheatre is a different monument from the theatre this entry names, so it cannot be used as the site's point. The field stays as it is.

No source that states the value dates this theatre's start. English Wikipedia names the monument but gives no year for it ('A stadium and a theatre lie outside the walls to the south'), and the pages found for the site are guides to the whole Anavarza archaeological site rather than a dating of the theatre, so the field stays empty.

No page was found that documents this theatre as a site of its own: the English Wikipedia article, the Turkish Museums page and the Turkish Culture Portal page all cover the whole Anavarza archaeological site, and the earlier pass's pages for the theatre of Ankara and of İznik are different sites. The field stays empty.

English and Spanish Wikipedia describe the Quillcay Machay paintings only as having later Chavinoid influence, with no year, century or millennium; no other readable source dates the site.

The stone is a natural basalt boulder; German Wikipedia and Czech Wikipedia give only the legend that Hotu Matu'a brought it, and the present arrangement dates from the 1960s. No source dates a start of the site as a year, century or millennium.

The only point for the Temnin el-Fawqa sanctuary (the nymphaeum of Ain el-Jobb) is Vici's pin, and its own annotation says the location is uncertain (Aliquot places it 500 m west of the village, Taylor only 'a 20 minute walk up the valley'); Wikipedia prints only the village's point, so no source gives a firm point for the site.
No page found dates the Temnin el-Fawqa sanctuary or nymphaeum; the Wikipedia and Vici pages give only 'Roman' without a year or century.

Wikipedia only calls Alagonia an ancient town of Messenia taken from Pausanias; Pleiades and ToposText give only the attestation periods Classical to Roman (550 BC - AD 300 as attested range), which is a period range for when the place is attested, not a dated foundation or start of the site.

No readable source prints a point for the Craterus monument itself; the Wikipedia article and its Commons category give none, and the Commons file pages only carry photographers' camera positions, which are not a site point.

English and Spanish Wikipedia describe the Chawaytiri rock paintings without any date; the one page that says Inca era (a scribd upload) gives only a period word, and the MINCETUR-restating page is behind a bot challenge. No year, century or millennium is attested.
Spanish Wikipedia states the culture and period of Llactan have not yet been determined; no source found dates it.

Neither the English Wikipedia article nor its Wikidata item prints a point for Quishuar (the article is listed as missing coordinates), and the MINCETUR record of Yanama only names Quishuar among the district's ruins; no readable source gives a quotable point.

The MINCETUR inventory says the Yanama ruins including Quishuar are pre-Inca but that their history is unknown for lack of study; Wikipedia gives no date. No year, century or millennium for the start.
Wikipedia and Wikidata give no point for Sitio Sierra; the Smithsonian STRI page gives only a grid reference (5379800E-9038500N), which is not read; no readable page prints geographic coordinates.
The Military Way is a long linear road along Hadrian's Wall; neither Wikipedia nor its Wikidata item gives a coordinate, and no source gives a point for the road as a whole.
The Ministerio de Cultura associates the site only with the Late Intermediate and Late Horizon periods and Wikipedia says pre-Inca; no year or century is given for its start.

No readable page prints a point for the Lefkaritis Tomb: Wikipedia and Wikidata carry none, the Hadjisavvas papers only give its street address (Vasileos Konstantinou 27, Larnaca), and no map or register page naming the tomb was found.

Wikipedia and Wikidata give no point for Pumamarka in San Sebastian; the stored point lies outside the bounding box of the Parque Arqueologico de Pumamarka and the only points found (OpenStreetMap hacienda node, park relation) are map-database values, not a quotable source for the site's centre.
The Cusco culture directorate and municipal pages call it a pre-Hispanic religious centre with Inca elements but give no year or century for its start.

The Wikidata item for the Phaselis Aqueduct records only its type, country, administrative location, conservation state and register IDs; it carries no inception or construction date, and no readable source I found dates this aqueduct.

The English and Albanian Wikipedia articles print no coordinates; the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire point is 1.7 km from the stored point and Pleiades cannot be read (bot challenge); no readable page prints a point for the harbour itself within 1 km.

Neither the English nor the French Wikipedia article for Mawk'allaqta (La Union, Puyca) prints a point, the Mincetur records found concern namesakes in Paruro and Sandia, and the Datahub copy lists longitude first; no quotable latitude-first point was found.
Wikipedia gives only 'about 500CE to 1000CE' as the span of the Wari culture that developed the site, a period range for the culture rather than a date for the start of this site.
